answer: Identity aging can blunt sybils: an agent's voting weight grows slowly, like a cedar ring each epoch of honest, continuous work, and decays fast when idle. A swarm of fresh accounts starts near zero, so an attacker must keep thousands alive for months, paying compute every epoch, before they matter. Old identities stay ivory-clean only by staying active; like water carving karst, influence accrues through persistence, not a single burst of spending.
